note:
Braids' TIMBRE is the shared shape knob (opens the saw's pw as it narrows the square's) and COLOR is the saw/square crossfade, so p1 maps to the engine's TIMBRE and p2 to its HARMONICS. MORPH and MACRO sit at noon in every case: at MORPH=0.5 the phase offset is zero (the module's own always-locked pair) and at MACRO=0.5 the square attenuation is Braids' fixed 0.578125. The blend-saw/blend-square pair is the one most likely to catch a parameter_[0]/parameter_[1] mix-up (fold's own trap): if COLOR were misread as TIMBRE, both cases would render a plausible-looking waveform but at the wrong pitch/shape entirely.

Every model-faithful case holds at the port's standard tolerance -- AC RMS within 1.0 dB, spectrum within 1.5 dB. Measured: AC RMS -0.11 to -0.01 dB and spectrum 0.32 to 0.48 dB across all six, mixed cases no worse than the isolated blend-saw/blend-square pair. The residual is entirely top-octave: every band below 5 kHz sits within +/-0.1 dB, while 10.24-20.48 kHz reads about -2 dB and 20.48-24 kHz -2 to -3 dB. That is R8 -- this port's float polyBLEP against Braids' int16 fixed-point BLEP -- not a mapping or a phase error. `clamp-square` is the one case carrying a wider tolerance, and its delta is the PORT's own declared pw clamp; see its note.

The module's own shape-change re-Init quirk does apply to this model, and costs nothing measurable because here it is COMMON-MODE. AnalogOscillator::Render calls Init() whenever shape_ != previous_shape_ (analog_oscillator.cc:75-78), and Init() resets pitch_ to 60 << 7 (analog_oscillator.h:77) AFTER RenderSawSquare has already called set_pitch -- so the module renders its first 24-sample block at MIDI 60 rather than at the played note, and the resulting phase error persists. But macro_oscillator.cc:136-137 sets BOTH oscillators' shapes on the same first Render, both differ from the zero-initialised previous_shape_ (OSC_SHAPE_SAW), so BOTH re-Init in that same block, both render block 0 at MIDI 60, and both ramp phase_increment_ up from the same zero previous_phase_increment_. The pair therefore stays in exact relative lock. Measured: cross-correlating the reference's saw-alone (p2 = 0) and square-alone (p2 = 1) renders at note 48 against this port's, both land at the SAME lag -- +330 samples, i.e. zero samples of relative offset -- at correlation 0.987 and 0.990 over a four-cycle window. This port does not reproduce the absolute offset the quirk leaves behind (24 * (f60 - fnote) / 96000 cycles: +0.038 at note 45, +0.033 at note 48, -0.196 at note 84), and does not need to: an absolute phase offset shared by both oscillators moves neither AC RMS nor the magnitude spectrum. The port's phase-locked pair (MORPH's own stock value) is the correct, intentional reading -- see saw_square_engine.h.

cases.name: The saw alone (COLOR at its floor)
The attenuated square alone (COLOR at its ceiling)
Shape at its ceiling: wide saw, a thin square sliver
cases.note2: TIMBRE 0.95 gives the saw pw 0.475 and the square pw 0.025 -- a thin low notch against a nearly-doubled saw. At note 48 the port's extra clamp floor is 2f = 0.0055, well under 0.025, so this case does NOT reach it. The same TIMBRE at note 84 does, and that is `clamp-square` below.

cases.name: Both waveforms evenly, mid shape
cases.note2: The mix most sensitive to relative saw-vs-square phase: HARMONICS = 0.5 with TIMBRE = 0.5 gives both waveforms their sharpest, most symmetric pw (0.25 apiece), so any phase error between the pair would show here first. It measures -0.01 dB AC RMS.

cases.name: Shape at its floor: narrow saw, wide square
cases.note2: The complement of timbre-high: TIMBRE 0.05 holds the saw at its 1024/65536 floor and opens the square to pw 0.475.

cases.name: Two octaves up, both waveforms evenly
cases.note2: The register where the module's shape-change re-Init quirk leaves its largest absolute offset (-0.196 cycles, two octaves away from the MIDI 60 the quirk resets to) -- and it still costs nothing, because the offset is common to both oscillators. This case also does NOT reach the port's extra pw clamp: at note 84 the frequency is 0.0219 cycles/sample so the clamp floor is 2f = 0.0437, and TIMBRE = 0.5 asks for pw = 0.25 on both oscillators. The clamp is covered by `clamp-square` below.

cases.name: The pw clamp, where it actually bites
cases.note2: The one case that exercises the engine's declared extra clamp, and the only one carrying a wider tolerance. COLOR = 1 so only the square is audible. Braids asks for square pw = (32768 - 0.95*32767)/65536 = 0.0250; at note 84 the port's 2*frequency floor raises it to 0.0437, a 75% wider low notch. That is the whole of the +2.42 dB AC RMS / 3.70 dB spectrum below -- a documented PORT deviation, measured rather than hidden. The pitch figure is a detector artefact: on a pulse this thin autocorrelation locks two octaves down, so `cents` is not asserted here.
